children.translated_text: <s>Adhyardhaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> (The Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred and Fifty [Lines])

body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to the Blessed <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>! Homage!

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān* * * * * * * vajrapāṇinā bodhisattvena mahāsattvena, avalokiteśvareṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena, ākāśagarbheṇa ca, vajramuṣṭinā ca, mañjuśriyā, ca sacittotpādadharmacakrapravarta(rti)nā(?) ca, gaganagañjena ca, sarvamārapramardinā ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena | evaṃpramukhairaṣṭābhirbodhisattvakoṭibhiḥ* * * ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇaṃ sadarthaṃ supadākṣaraṃ paryavadātam, sarvadharmaviśuddhinirhāraṃ deśayati sma - kāmaviśuddhipadametat yaduta bodhisattvapadam | dṛṣṭiviśuddhipadametat yaduta bodhisattvapadam | rativiśuddhipadametat yaduta bodhisattvapadam | tṛṣṇāviśuddhipadametat yaduta bodhisattvapadam | bhūṣaṇaviśuddhipadametat yaduta bodhisattvapadam | āhlādanaviśuddhipadametat yaduta bodhisattvapadam | ālokaviśuddhipadametat yaduta bodhisattvapadam | kāyasukhaviśuddhipadematat yaduta bodhisattvapadam |[vāksukha] viśuddhipadametat yaduta bodhisattvapadam | manoviśuddhipadametat yaduta bodhisattvapadam | śabdaviśuddhipadametat yaduta bodhisattvapadam | gandhaviśuddhipadametat yaduta bodhisattvapadam | rasaviśuddhipadametat yaduta bodhisattvapadam | sparśaviśuddhipadametat yaduta bodhisattvapadam | tatkasya hetoḥ? tadyathā sarvadharmāḥ svabhāvaviśuddhāḥ | sarvadharmāḥ [svabhāvaśūnyāḥ] | svabhāvaśūnyatayā prajñāpāramitāviśuddhirbhavati ||
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) [was dwelling] ... with the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, and <s>Ākāśagarbha</s>, and <s>Vajramuṣṭi</s>, and <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, and <s>Sacittotpādadharmacakrapravartin</s>, and <s>Gaganagañja</s>, and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvamārapramardin</s> — led by these, with eight <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> ... He was teaching — excellent at the beginning, excellent in the middle, excellent at the end, meaningful, with good words and syllables, completely pure — the extraction of the purification of all <s>dharmas</s>: 'The purification of desire (<s>kāma</s>) — this is the stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The purification of views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) — this is the stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The purification of delight (<s>rati</s>) — this is the stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The purification of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) — this is the stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The purification of adornment (<s>bhūṣaṇa</s>) — this is the stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The purification of delight (<s>āhlādana</s>) — this is the stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The purification of light (<s>āloka</s>) — this is the stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The purification of bodily happiness (<s>kāyasukha</s>) — this is the stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The purification of speech-happiness (<s>vāksukha</s>) — this is the stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The purification of mind (<s>manas</s>) — this is the stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The purification of sound (<s>śabda</s>) — this is the stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The purification of smell (<s>gandha</s>) — this is the stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The purification of taste (<s>rasa</s>) — this is the stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The purification of touch (<s>sparśa</s>) — this is the stage of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' What is the reason? Namely: all <s>dharmas</s> are pure by own-nature. All <s>dharmas</s> are empty by own-nature. Through own-nature emptiness, the purification of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> comes about.

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanastathāgataḥ punarapīdaṃ prajñāpāramitānayaṃ sarvatathāgataśāntadharmatābhisaṃbodhinirhāraṃ deśayati sma - vajrasamatābhisaṃbodhi(dhau?) mahābodhivajradṛḍhatayā | arthasamatābhisaṃbodhau mahābodhirekārthatayā | dharmasamatābhisaṃbodhau mahābodhiḥ svabhāvaśuddhatayā(?) | sarvasamatābhisaṃbodhau mahābodhiḥ sarvāvikalpanatayeti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vairocana</s> again taught this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> method — the extraction of the awakening to the peaceful nature of all <s>dharmas</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>: 'In the awakening to the equality of the <s>vajra</s> (diamond), great awakening is through the firmness of the <s>vajra</s>. In the awakening to the equality of meaning, great awakening is through the oneness of meaning. In the awakening to the equality of <s>dharma</s>, great awakening is through purity of own-nature. In the awakening to the equality of all, great awakening is through the non-conceptualization of all.'

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvaduṣṭavinayaśākyamunistathāgataḥ punarapi sarvadharmasamatāvijayasaṃgrahaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitānirhāraṃ deśayāmāsa - rāgāprapañcatayā* * * | dveṣāprapañcatayā* * * mohāprapañcatā, mohāprapañcatayā sarvadharmāprapañcatā, sarvadharmāprapañcatayā prajñāpāramitāprapañcatā veditavyā iti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, Subduer of All the Wicked, again taught the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> extraction called 'Victory and Gathering of the Equality of All <s>Dharmas</s>': 'Through the non-elaboration of passion (<s>rāga</s>) ... through the non-elaboration of hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) ... the non-elaboration of delusion (<s>moha</s>); through the non-elaboration of delusion, the non-elaboration of all <s>dharmas</s>; through the non-elaboration of all <s>dharmas</s>, the non-elaboration of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood.'

children.text: ) atha bhagavān svabhāvaśuddhastathāgataḥ punarapīdaṃ sarvadharmasamatāvalokiteśvarajñānamudraṃ nāma prajñāpāramitānayaṃ deśayāmāsa - sarvarāgaviśuddhitā loke dveṣaviśuddhitāyai saṃvartate | sarvamalaviśuddhitā loke dveṣavi[śu]ddhitāyai saṃvartate | sarvamalaviśuddhitā loke sarvapāpaviśuddhitāyai saṃvartate | sarvadharmaviśuddhitā loke sarvasattvaviśuddhitāyai saṃvartate | sarvajñānaviśuddhitā loke prajñāpāramitāviśuddhyai saṃvartate iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Svabhāvaśuddha</s> (Pure by Own-Nature) again taught this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> method called 'The Knowledge-Seal of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> [Arising from] the Equality of All <s>Dharmas</s>': 'The purification of all passion in the world leads to the purification of hatred. The purification of all defilement in the world leads to the purification of all sin. The purification of all <s>dharmas</s> in the world leads to the purification of all beings. The purification of all knowledge in the world leads to the purification of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatraidhātukādhipatistathāgataḥ punarapi sarvatathāgatābhiṣekasaṃbhavajñānagarbhaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitānayaṃ deśayāmāsa - abhiṣekadānaṃ sarvatraidhātukarājyapratilambhāya saṃvartate | arthadānaṃ sarvāśāparipūraye saṃvartate | dharmadānaṃ sarvadharmatāprāptaye saṃvartate | āmiṣadānaṃ sarvakāyavākcittasukhapratilambhāya saṃvartate iti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s>, Lord of All Three Realms, again taught this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> method called 'The Womb of Knowledge Arising from the Consecration of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>': 'The gift of consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) leads to the attainment of sovereignty over all three realms. The gift of benefit (<s>arthadāna</s>) leads to the fulfillment of all wishes. The gift of <s>Dharma</s> leads to the attainment of the nature of all <s>dharmas</s>. The gift of material things (<s>āmiṣadāna</s>) leads to the attainment of the happiness of body, speech, and mind.'

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatajñānamudrāprāptasarvatathāgatamuṣṭidharastathāgataḥ [śāśvata](?) punarapi sarvatathāgatajñānamudrādhiṣṭhānavajraṃ nāma prajñāpāramitānayaṃ deśayāmāsa - sarvatathāgatakāyamudrāparigrahaḥ sarvatathāgatatvāya saṃvartate | vāgmudrāparigrahaḥ sarvadharmapratilambhāya saṃvartate | cittamudrāparigrahaḥ sarvasamādhipratilambhāya saṃvartate | vajramudrāpratigrahaḥ sarvakāyavākcittavajrasattvasarvottamasiddhaye saṃvartate iti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> who holds the fist of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having attained the wisdom-seal (<s>jñānamudrā</s>) of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, taught again the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> method called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Wisdom-Seal of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>: The embracing of the body-seal (<s>kāyamudrā</s>) of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> leads to the state of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. The embracing of the speech-seal (<s>vāgmudrā</s>) leads to the attainment of all <s>dharmas</s>. The embracing of the mind-seal (<s>cittamudrā</s>) leads to the attainment of all <s>samādhis</s>. The embracing of the <s>vajra</s>-seal (<s>vajramudrā</s>) leads to the supreme <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) of the <s>vajrasattva</s> (adamantine being) of all body, speech, and mind.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvadharmāprapañcastathāgataḥ punarapi cakrākṣaraparivartaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitānayaṃ deśayāmāsa - śūnyāḥ sarvadharmā niḥsvabhāvayogena, nirnimittāḥ sarvadharmā nirnimittatāmupādāya, apraṇihitāḥ sarvadharmā apraṇidhānayogena, prakṛtiprabhāsvarāḥ prajñāpāramitāpariśuddhyā iti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> of the Non-Elaboration of All Dharmas, taught again the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> method called the Revolution of the <s>Cakra</s>-Syllable: All <s>dharmas</s> are empty (<s>śūnya</s>) through the yoga of essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>). All <s>dharmas</s> are signless (<s>nirnimitta</s>) by virtue of the absence of signs. All <s>dharmas</s> are without aspiration (<s>apraṇihita</s>) through the yoga of non-aspiration. All <s>dharmas</s> are luminous by nature (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvara</s>) through the purification of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvatathāgatacakrāntargatastathāgataḥ punarapi mahācakrapraveśaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitānayaṃ deśayāmāsa - vajrasamatāpraveśaḥ sarvatathāgatacakrapraveśāya saṃvartate | arthasamatāpraveśo mahābodhisattvacakrapraveśāya saṃvartate | dharmasamatāpraveśaḥ sarvadharmacakrapraveśāya saṃvartate | sarvasamatāpraveśaḥ sarvacakrapraveśāya saṃvartate iti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> Entered into the <s>Cakra</s> of All <s>Tathāgatas</s>, taught again the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> method called the Entry into the Great <s>Cakra</s>: Entry into the equality of the <s>vajra</s> (<s>vajrasamatā</s>) leads to entry into the <s>cakra</s> of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Entry into the equality of meaning (<s>arthasamatā</s>) leads to entry into the <s>cakra</s> of the great <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Entry into the equality of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmasamatā</s>) leads to entry into the <s>cakra</s> of all <s>dharmas</s>. Entry into the equality of all (<s>sarvasamatā</s>) leads to entry into all <s>cakras</s>.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvapūjāvidhivistarabhājanastathāgataḥ punarapi sarvapūjāgryaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitānayaṃ deśayāmāsa - bodhicittotpādanatā sarvatathāgatapūjāvidhivistaraḥ | sarvasattvadhātuparitrāṇatā sarvatathāgatapūjāvidhivistaraḥ | saddharmaparigrahaḥ sarvatathāgatapūjāvidhivistaraḥ | prajñāpāramitālikhanalekhanadhāraṇavācanoccāraṇabhāvanapūjanakarmaṇa(karma?) sarvatathāgatapūjāvidhivistaraḥ iti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> Who Is the Vessel of the Elaboration of All Worship Rites, taught again the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> method called the Supreme of All Worship: The generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) is the elaboration of the worship rite of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. The protection of the entire realm of beings is the elaboration of the worship rite of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. The upholding of the true <s>Dharma</s> is the elaboration of the worship rite of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. The acts of writing, copying, retaining, reciting, chanting, contemplating, and worshipping the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> constitute the elaboration of the worship rite of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān sarvavinayasamarthastathāgataḥ punarapīdaṃ jñānamuṣṭiparigrahaṃ sarva[sa]ttvavinayajñānagarbhaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitānayaṃ deśayāmāsa - sarvasattvasamatāyāṃ krodhasamatā, sarvasattvavinayanatāyāṃ krodhavinayanatā, sarvasattvadharmatāyāṃ krodhadharmatā, sarvasattvavajratāyāṃ krodhavajratā | tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvasattvavinayo bodhiriti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> Capable of All Discipline, taught again the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> method called the Womb of Knowledge for the Discipline of All Beings, the Embrace of the Fist of Knowledge: In the equality of all beings there is the equality of wrath (<s>krodha</s>). In the discipline of all beings there is the discipline of wrath. In the true nature (<s>dharmatā</s>) of all beings there is the true nature of wrath. In the adamantine nature (<s>vajratā</s>) of all beings there is the adamantine nature of wrath. For what reason? Because the discipline of all beings is <s>bodhi</s> (awakening).

children.text: ) atha bhagavān sarvadharmasamatāpratiṣṭhitastathāgataḥ punarapīdaṃ sarvadharmāgryaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitānayaṃ deśayāmāsa - sarvasamatayā prajñāpāramitāsamatā, sarvārthatayā prajñāpāramitārthatā, sarvadharmatayā prajñāpāramitādharmatā, sarvakarmatayā prajñāpāramitākarmatā veditavyā iti ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> Established in the Equality of All Dharmas, taught again the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> method called the Supreme of All Dharmas: Through the equality of all, the equality of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> [is to be known]. Through the purposefulness of all, the purposefulness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Through the true nature of all, the true nature of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Through the activity of all, the activity of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is to be known.

body.text: atha bhagavāṃstathāgato vairocanaḥ punarapi sarvasattvādhiṣṭhānaṃ nāma prajñāpāramitānayaṃ deśayāmāsa - sarvasattvāstathāgatagarbhāḥ samantabhadramahābodhisattvasarvātmatayo(yā?) | vajragarbhā sarvasattvā vajragarbhābhiṣiktatayā, dharmagarbhāḥ sarvasattvāḥ sarvavākpravartanatayā, karmagarbhāḥ sarvasattvāḥ sarvasattvakaraṇatāprayogatayā iti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vairocana</s>, taught again the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> method called the Empowerment of All Beings: All beings possess the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> (womb/embryo of the <s>Tathāgata</s>), because they are of the very nature of <s>Samantabhadra</s>, the great <s>Bodhisattva</s>. All beings possess the <s>vajra</s>-embryo (<s>vajragarbha</s>), because they are consecrated with the <s>vajra</s>-embryo. All beings possess the <s>dharma</s>-embryo (<s>dharmagarbha</s>), because of the operation of all speech. All beings possess the action-embryo (<s>karmagarbha</s>), because of the application of the activity for all beings.

body.text: atha bhagavānanantāparyantāniṣṭhastathāgato 'nantāparyantāniṣṭhadharmā punarapyasya kalpasya pariniṣṭhādhiṣṭhānārthamidaṃ sarvadharmasamatāparininadhiṣṭhānavajraṃ nāma prajñāpāramitānayaṃ deśayāmāsaprajñāpāramitānantatayā sarvatathāgatānantatā, prajñāpāramitāparyantatayā sarvatathāgatāparyantatā, prajñāpāramitānaikatayā sarvadharmānaikatā, prajñāpāramitāpariniṣṭhatayā sarvadharmāpariniṣṭhatā bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> of Infinite and Boundless Completion, whose <s>dharmas</s> are infinite, boundless, and complete, for the purpose of empowering the completion of this <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), taught again the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> method called the Vajra of the Empowerment of the Equality and Completion of All Dharmas: Through the infinitude of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, all <s>Tathāgatas</s> are infinite. Through the boundlessness of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, all <s>Tathāgatas</s> are boundless. Through the non-singularity of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are non-singular. Through the completion of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the completion of all <s>dharmas</s> comes to be.

body.text: atha bhagavān vairocanaḥ sarvatathāgataguhyadharmatāprāptasarvadharmāprapañcaḥ punarapi idaṃ mahāsukhavajrāmogha* * * nāma vajrāmoghadharmatāprajñāpāramitāmukhaṃ paramamanādinidhanamadhyaṃ deśayāmāsa - mahārogottamasiddhirmahābodhisattvānāṃ mahāsukhottamasiddhyai saṃvartate | mahāsukhottamasiddhirmahābodhisattvānāṃ sarvatathāgatamahābodhyuttamasiddhyai saṃvartate | sarvatathāgatamahābodhyuttamasiddhirmahābodhisattvānāṃ sarvamahāmārapramardanottamasiddhyai saṃvartate | sarvamahāmārapramardanottamasiddhirmahābodhisattvānāṃ sakalamahātraidhātukaiśvaryottamasiddhyai saṃvartate | sakalamahātraidhātukaiśvaryottamasiddhirmahābodhisattvānāmaśeṣānavaśeṣasarvasattvadhātuparitrāṇasarvasattvahita - sukhaparamātyantamahāsukhottamasiddhyai saṃvartate iti || tatkasya hetoḥ?
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One <s>Vairocana</s>, having attained the secret <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, [whose] all <s>dharmas</s> are without elaboration, taught again the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> method called the Great Bliss Vajra Amoghā... <s>Vajrāmoghadharmatā-Prajñāpāramitā</s>, which is supremely without beginning, end, or middle: 'The supreme <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) of great rapture leads for great <s>bodhisattvas</s> to the supreme <s>siddhi</s> of great bliss (<s>mahāsukha</s>). The supreme <s>siddhi</s> of great bliss leads for great <s>bodhisattvas</s> to the supreme <s>siddhi</s> of the great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>) of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. The supreme <s>siddhi</s> of the great awakening of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> leads for great <s>bodhisattvas</s> to the supreme <s>siddhi</s> of crushing all great <s>Māras</s>. The supreme <s>siddhi</s> of crushing all great <s>Māras</s> leads for great <s>bodhisattvas</s> to the supreme <s>siddhi</s> of complete sovereign mastery over the great three realms (<s>tridhātu</s>). The supreme <s>siddhi</s> of complete sovereign mastery over the great three realms leads for great <s>bodhisattvas</s> to the supreme <s>siddhi</s> of the ultimate, absolute great bliss of the complete protection of the entire realm of all beings without remainder and without exception, and of the welfare and happiness of all beings.' For what reason?

children.translated_text: As long as there are excellent heroes empowered in existence,
so long are they, not having entered <s>nirvāṇa</s>, able to accomplish the incomparable welfare of beings. // 1 //
Accomplished through the empowerment of wisdom, means, and knowledge of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,
through the purification of all actions, they become purified in [their engagement with] existence. // 2 //
The discipline of passion and the like in the world [is applied] throughout existence, for themselves, constantly and always;

children.text: teṣāṃ viśodhanārthaṃ tu vinayaṃ jñātavān svayam || 3 ||
children.translated_text: for the purpose of purifying those [beings], he himself has known the discipline. // 3 //

children.text: yathā padmaṃ suraktaṃ tu rāgadoṣairna lipyate |
children.translated_text: Just as a lotus, brilliantly red, is not stained by the faults of passion,
so those [bodhisattvas], dwelling always in existence for the welfare of the world, are not stained by its faults. // 4 //

body.text:
mahārāgaviśuddhāstu mahāsaukhyā mahādhanāḥ |
tridhātvīśvaratāṃ prāptā arthaṃ kurvantu taṃ dṛḍham || 5 ||iti ||
body.translated_text:
Purified by great passion, of great bliss, of great wealth,
having attained sovereign mastery over the three realms, may they firmly accomplish that [welfare of beings]! // 5 //
The <s>Adhyardhaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred and Fifty [Verses]) is completed.
